chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Ja'far b. Bashir al-Bajali narrated to us, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman b. A'yan, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
that he said: Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgave a man from the people of the desert because of two phrases he supplicated with.
He said: 'O Allah! If You punish me, then I am worthy of that, but if You forgive me, then You are worthy of that.'

key_terms.أهل البادية: People of the desert (bedouin), often seen as simple folk whose sincerity is praised
key_terms.أهل ذلك: Worthy of that / deserving of that — used in both clauses to create a powerful rhetorical balance

ai.seo_question: What is the famous supplication of the bedouin that earned Allah's forgiveness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir relates that a bedouin man was forgiven by Allah simply through a heartfelt supplication. The man acknowledged God's justice in punishing him while also recognizing God's inherent worthiness of showing mercy. This hadith, narrated in the scholarly circles of 4th-century Qom, emphasizes that sincere recognition of one's lowliness before God's majesty is the essence of effective supplication.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Bashir al-Bajali narrated to us from Aban from `Abd al-Rahman b. A`yan from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as).

He said: Allah forgave a man from the people of the desert because of two phrases he would supplicate with: “O Allah! If You punish me, then that is what I deserve, but if You forgive me, then that is what You deserve (Allahumma in tu`adhibani fa ahl dhalik ana, wa in tughfir li fa ahl dhalik anta).”
